newsitem.title: RUSSIA: EU subsidy not hitting US grain exports - Goldthwait.
newsitem.headline: EU subsidy not hitting US grain exports - Goldthwait.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department General Sales Manager Chris Goldthwait said in Moscow on Friday that EU grain export subsidies were not affecting U.S. grain export volumes.

"We do not believe that in terms of quantity, the current EU subsidies are actually cutting into our own exports from the United States," he said in a brief telephone interview. "In today's market conditions, we are basically selling what we have available for export from the U.S., so we don't think there's a big impact from the EU subsidisation on current sales out of the U.S."
But he said he saw no reason for export subsidies per se and added that the EU subsidies were pressuring prices.
"We do not see any reason to be subsidising grain exports under current market conditions," he said.

"There's probably a little bit of price dampening effect which we do not like to see, and you know, frankly, we just don't see any reason why anyone should be using export subsidies in today's market."
But he noted that the European Union had progressively reduced subsidies in recent weeks.
Goldthwait was in Moscow for a visit after meeting European Union officials in Brussels earlier this week.
